quote_repairs.replacement_quote: Solving a nonlinear integral equation generally requires some iterative procedure, where an initial guess is refined iteratively. Since the evaluation of z at time t requires evaluation of z at all time points between 0 and t due to the integral ∫ t 0 G ( z s , t, s ) ds . Observe that once an approximation (guess) z j ( t ) has been obtained, all evaluations happen in parallel for each iteration, since we can integrate using z j ( t ) , see Zappala et al. (2024) for details. We present the model with sequences starting from the initial state z 0 and extending to various lengths (e.g., predicting from z 0 to z 1 , z 0 to z 2 , up to z 0 to z N ). This trains the model on multiple sub-trajectories, which can be used in inference in an iterative manner to output the complete trajectory.
